scenes.subtitle: The Blueprint Copying Process of Life
scenes.narration: Welcome to this presentation on DNA replication — the fascinating biological process that ensures every new cell receives an exact copy of life's blueprint, the DNA molecule.

scenes.caption: DNA replication is the process by which a cell makes an identical copy of its DNA before cell division.
scenes.narration: At its core, DNA replication is about accuracy and precision. Each cell must duplicate its DNA so that when it divides, both daughter cells carry the same genetic code.
Various enzymes play key roles in DNA replication. This chart shows their relative activity levels during the process.
DNA replication occurs in three main stages: initiation, elongation, and termination. Each stage is crucial for accurate duplication.
The DNA strands are antiparallel, meaning one is copied smoothly while the other is made in short fragments, both ensuring complete replication.
Replication consumes cellular energy in the form of ATP. Here is how energy is distributed across major steps.
Replication is teamwork at the molecular level. Enzymes like helicase, primase, polymerase, and ligase work in perfect coordination.
Here’s a simple pseudo-code representation. Each base in DNA has a complement: A pairs with T, and G pairs with C. The program simulates how new strands are built.

scenes.text: 3D Model of the DNA Double Helix
scenes.narration: This 3D helix visualization represents the twisting beauty of DNA’s double structure — two strands linked by complementary bases.

scenes.quote: DNA is like a computer program but far, far more advanced than any software ever created.
scenes.author: Bill Gates
scenes.narration: This quote reminds us how intricate and efficient DNA truly is — a natural code written billions of years ago, still running flawlessly today.

scenes.question: Which enzyme joins Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand?
scenes.answerText: Correct! DNA ligase seals the gaps between Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand.

scenes.narration: Before we conclude, here are the key points to remember. DNA replication ensures the faithful transmission of genetic information across generations.

scenes.subtitle: DNA – The Code That Defines Life
scenes.narration: Thank you for exploring DNA replication with us. This process is at the heart of life’s continuity — the molecular bridge between generations.
